gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $35 Furbo Mini 360° is $118.92 at furbo.com checkout once its bundled first-year Nanny plan ($83.92) is added, which is over the shopper's $100 budget; the camera-only price is $99, and that buys a hopper Furbo itself rates at 'up to 10 small treats'.
standout_why: Rival pages compared: VettedFur (cited in five of the seven runs), HomeGearLab (cited once, 2026-11-13), and TheConsumers.guide (cited in four runs). WIRED and Good Housekeeping would not open. HomeGearLab already says the Mini 360° is '$35 with a Furbo Nanny plan', lists the camera alone at $99, and says it 'holds up to 10 small treats', so the core of the finding is already on a page ChatGPT cited. None of the rivals gives the $118.92 checkout total. VettedFur gives two-year costs for the Furbo 360°, Petcube and SKYMEE but has no price for the Mini 360° (out of stock when it checked). TheConsumers.guide does not cover the Mini 360° at all and already prices the TKENPRO at $89.99. ChatGPT itself showed the Mini 360° as '$30–$49 promotional', and the TKENPRO at 'about $70' in three runs, about $70–90 in one and about $90 in the latest two.
decides: This confirms the Petcube Bites 2 Lite as the pick. It is $79.99 on Amazon today ($99.99 at petcube.com), needs no plan, and holds 1.5 lb of treats. The only Furbo with treat tossing that gets near $100 is the Mini 360°, which costs either $118.92 with the plan at furbo.com, $99 as a camera alone, or $99 on Amazon with a 6-month plan. Every one of those holds 10 treats. The TKENPRO is not the bargain ChatGPT showed: it is $85.49–$89.99 on Amazon today, not $70. The WOPET that ChatGPT searched for is now a 6 L food feeder at $105.99 with no treat tossing.
